To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) a single A/D for all GNSS signals can be used in a multi-band receiver, and 2) a digitalization scheme that includes a decimator and requantizer can be implemented in the same way as in the case of separate converters.
a single A/D for all signals can be used with a negligible performance loss, and the digitalization scheme can be further improved by adding a digital filter and decimator, followed by a requantizer.
a joint digitalization scheme for a multi-band GNSS receiver is feasible, but the degradation in performance with respect to a classic scheme is of the order of a few decibels.

the design of digital filters for the processing of GNSS signals.

the design of a digitalization scheme that allows the implementation of a multi-band GNSS receiver employing a single A.D converter for all signals, with a performance similar to that of a classic scheme with several A/D converters.
the design of the digital front-end of a multi-band GNSS receiver, in order to obtain the maximum performance with a single ADC.

a single converter scheme for multiband receivers is a feasible solution, but it is not as attractive as the separate converters scheme in terms of performance.
the proposed scheme allows the use of a single A/D for the reception of all the signals, at the cost of a small loss in the signal to noise ratio.

a joint digitalization scheme is possible and can be used in practice for multiband GNASS receivers, with a degradation in performance of about 1 dB, but with a significant simplification of the implementation.

the proposed joint digitalization scheme for GNSS multiband receivers can be a good trade-off between the classic separate converters scheme and a single converter scheme without any filtering or digitalization, which would be the simplest solution but would imply a loss of about 10 dB in the signal to noise ratio.
, in the case study, a joint digitalization scheme with a single A/D for GPS and GLONAS signals is feasible, and that it can be implemented with a small loss in performance.

a digitalization scheme employing a single A.D. converter can be used to reduce the number of A.D. converters and to simplify the implementation of a multi-band GNSS receiver.
a joint digitalization scheme can be used to reduce complexity in the design of multi-band receivers.
a joint scheme can be used in a multiband GNSS receiver, with an acceptable degradation, and with the advantage of reducing the number of converters and the complexity of the receiver.
